featured_videos.title: Let's Chat: My Transition Back To Carnivore
featured_videos.creator: Carnivore Quest
featured_videos.editorial_title: Let's Chat: My Transition Back To Carnivore
featured_videos.commentary: This is what real progress looks like, and honestly it's way more interesting than the highlight reel. Cassie's talking about the actual month, the struggles, what didn't work, and then showing up to try again. That's the stuff nobody posts but everyone needs to see. The comments are killing me too, because it's not "you're doing it wrong" energy, it's people saying "I'm on Day 1 and your honesty is keeping me here," and that matters way more than any perfect transformation. The keto-to-carnivore shift she's exploring is something a lot of people cycle through, and watching her troubleshoot what works for her body instead of forcing one rigid approach is exactly how this actually works in real life.

featured_videos.title: 6 Tiny Carnivore Rules That ACTUALLY Give You Your Waist Back Quickly (140lbs Lost)
featured_videos.creator: Carnivore Claire
featured_videos.editorial_title: 6 Tiny Carnivore Rules That ACTUALLY Give You Your Waist Back Quickly (140lbs Lost)
featured_videos.commentary: I love that someone pointed out "we all love on our own terms" because that's the real takeaway here, not just the six rules themselves. Claire's talking about 140 pounds, and the comments are full of people saying they've lost 66, 50, more. and what I keep hearing is that the "rules" only stick when they match how you actually live. I've seen this over and over in the years I've been around this space: the person who white-knuckles through perfection for three months crashes hard, but the one who picks the three things that feel doable? That's who keeps the weight off. The brutal honesty in her video (and the comments calling it out) is that there's no magic sequencing. just consistency on whatever version you can sustain. That's worth more than any perfect protocol.

featured_videos.title: Lion Diet for 30 Days: My DEXA Scan Was Disappointing
featured_videos.creator: HomeSteadHow
featured_videos.editorial_title: Lion Diet for 30 Days: My DEXA Scan Was Disappointing
featured_videos.commentary: The community's already onto something the DEXA didn't capture, and they're not wrong about it. People are zooming in on the skin clarity, the inflammation drop, the energy shift. stuff that shows up in your face before it shows up on a body composition scan. That 30-day window is honestly too short to move the needle on bone density or muscle mass in a meaningful way, which is why the comments are asking for the 90-day retest. The real story here isn't the disappointing numbers, it's that people are seeing him look and feel fundamentally different on beef alone, and they're recognizing something they want for themselves too.

featured_videos.title: What Happened After 365 Days of Eating Only Meat?
featured_videos.creator: High Calorie Human
featured_videos.editorial_title: What Happened After 365 Days of Eating Only Meat?
featured_videos.commentary: One year in and the thing that jumps out from the comments isn't just the weight or the energy, it's the gout reversal. That's not small. Someone in the comments nailed it, too, saying high uric acid gets blamed when fructose and processed carbs are actually the driver. I've covered this before with how sodium actually works on carnivore, but it's the same pattern, right, we blame the nutrient when the problem is what we stopped eating. This is exactly the kind of real-world data that matters more than any study sitting in a lab.

If you've been chasing the "dessert that doesn't sabotage you" problem, this one solves it without the usual carnivore recipe complexity.

featured_videos.title: These Carnivore Foods Are WAY Overrated
featured_videos.creator: Jenny Mitich
featured_videos.editorial_title: These Carnivore Foods Are WAY Overrated
featured_videos.commentary: Jenny's hitting something real here that doesn't get talked about enough: just because a food is carnivore doesn't mean it's your food. Look at the comment from someone who gained weight adding dairy back in and then spent three months fighting the food noise again. That's not weakness, that's biology. The person who went from 248 to 226 in two months and is now questioning whether they need that much butter while cooking. that's someone actually paying attention to their own results instead of copying what someone else does on YouTube. What matters most is finding your version that works, not nailing some perfect macro ratio that leaves you feeling worse. The butter obsession in the early days is real (I see it constantly), but so is the relief when people realize they can eat less of it and still feel full. That's not failure, that's progress.
